subject.title: fix(gateway): restrict backend self-pairing shared auth

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally stop preserving self-declared backend scopes for direct-loopback shared token/password clients, and if so with what upgrade posture?
rationale: Current docs, tests, and the latest release describe the existing behavior, so this security hardening needs an explicit Gateway/security boundary decision rather than routine repair automation.

options.title: Rebase and accept fail-closed behavior
options.body: Resolve conflicts while preserving current auth paths, then merge only with explicit acceptance that shared token/password no longer preserves backend scopes.

options.title: Add a transition path first
options.body: If shipped backend callers depend on this behavior, add a tested warning, migration, or compatibility window before the fail-closed change lands.

options.title: Pause for broader auth design
options.body: If maintainers want to revisit the trusted-loopback operator model, pause this PR in favor of a broader Gateway auth design item.

recommendation.title: Rebase and accept fail-closed behavior
recommendation.body: Resolve conflicts while preserving current auth paths, then merge only with explicit acceptance that shared token/password no longer preserves backend scopes.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent shared-token scope-clearing and Gateway credential-runtime history make this the best evidenced individual routing candidate for the auth-boundary decision.
